blocks.title: Export support across East Africa
blocks.body: Kenya remains the main logistics anchor through the Port of Mombasa, JKIA and regional corridors, but many export files involve cargo originating from neighbouring East African markets. Kenya Tradex helps coordinate documentation, routing and freight handover where cargo moves from inland producers, regional warehouses or cross-border suppliers into international or regional export channels.

Coordination for cargo originating from Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, DRC or South Sudan where routing, documents and border steps must be aligned.

blocks.title: What Kenya Tradex handles
blocks.body: Export cargo can move smoothly when the commercial file, customs entry, carrier booking, origin requirements and destination requirements are aligned before cargo is handed over. We help exporters prepare the file early so the shipment does not get slowed down at the point of departure or border movement.
items: Commercial invoice, packing list and cargo description review.
Export customs entry and customs release coordination.
Certificate of Origin and rules-of-origin support where required.
Product-specific permits, inspection or certificates depending on the cargo and destination.
Air freight, sea freight, road freight and cargo handover planning.
A practical export clearance partner anchored in Kenya and regional corridors.
Freight booking through JKIA, Mombasa or regional corridors.
Document checks before cargo is dispatched.
Guidance on customs, origin documents and destination requirements.

blocks.title: Export clearance process
steps:
Review the buyer, cargo and destination. 
We check the exporter's invoice, packing details, HS code direction, destination country and special requirements before shipment planning is locked.

Prepare the export customs file. 
The export entry, supporting documents and any required origin or product certificates are aligned with the shipment and carrier plan.

Coordinate freight and cargo handover. 
We plan air, sea or road movement, carrier cut-off times, cargo collection, consolidation, warehouse handling and delivery to the departure point.

Keep the exporter informed. 
Exporters receive practical updates on documentation, release, handover and movement so the buyer relationship stays protected.

blocks.title: Common export problems we help prevent
blocks.body: Some products and markets require origin, quality, health, phytosanitary or other certificates. These should be checked before cargo reaches the carrier cut-off.
paragraphs: Airline and vessel cut-off times can be unforgiving. Early freight planning protects bookings, buyer timelines and temperature-sensitive cargo.
Exports by road, air and sea each need different documents, handling and timing. The route should match the product, buyer terms and destination requirements.

faq.question: What documents are commonly needed to export cargo from Kenya and East Africa?
faq.answer: Common export documents include a commercial invoice, packing list, export customs entry, transport document, certificate of origin where required and product-specific permits or certificates depending on the cargo and destination country.

faq.question: Can Kenya Tradex support exports from Kenya and the rest of East Africa?
faq.answer: Yes. Kenya Tradex supports export cargo from Kenya and regional East African markets moving by air through JKIA and other gateways, by sea through the Port of Mombasa, and by road through regional trade corridors.

faq.question: When should an exporter start preparing customs documentation?
faq.answer: Exporters should start before cargo is packed or dispatched where possible. Early review helps confirm the buyer details, HS code, destination requirements, permits, certificate of origin needs and freight booking deadlines.
